title: Views & Updatable Views
description: Encapsulate complex SQL with Views, understand query inlining, and modify underlying tables via Updatable Views.

data.text: A **View** is a saved query that acts as a virtual table. It does not store physical data; whenever you query a view, PostgreSQL merges the view's query definition directly into the parent query plan during rewriting.
Creating a View with Security Boundaries

data.title: Exposing Non-Sensitive User Data
data.content: Hides password hashes and internal flags from reporting users.
data.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW public_users_view AS
SELECT 
    id,
    name,
    email,
    created_at
FROM users
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

data.text: Updatable Views and WITH CHECK OPTION

A simple view over one table, with no aggregates, `DISTINCT`, or window functions, is automatically updatable: `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE` against the view are rewritten against the base table. `WITH CHECK OPTION` prevents writes that would fall outside the view's own filter and disappear the next time you query it.

data.title: An updatable, self-protecting view
data.content: Only active employees are visible; an insert or update that sets `active = false` is rejected by the check option.
data.code:
CREATE VIEW active_employees AS
SELECT id, name, department, active
FROM employees
WHERE active = true
WITH CHECK OPTION;

UPDATE active_employees
SET department = 'Platform'
WHERE id = 7;          -- succeeds

UPDATE active_employees
SET active = false
WHERE id = 7;          -- ERROR: new row violates check option

data.title: Views use the owner's privileges by default
data.text: Before PostgreSQL 15 a view ran with the privileges of its owner, which made it a simple way to expose a subset of a table to a role with no direct table access. PostgreSQL 15 added `security_invoker = true`, which runs the view with the caller's privileges instead. Know which model your version uses before treating a view as a security boundary.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Views simplify complex multi-table queries and enforce security boundaries.
Views do not duplicate physical data on disk; queries are inlined at runtime.
Simple single-table views without aggregates are automatically updatable.
